key_insight: The paper shows that counterfactual simulator rollouts can be used to forecast outcomes under a new decision policy before real-world data from that policy exists. In short, it tackles the cold-start problem by using simulation to bridge the gap between past behavior and future deployment.
problem_solved: When a model’s targets depend on actions taken by a policy, historical data reflects older policies and does not match the new policy we want to evaluate. This creates a cold-start challenge for forecasting and policy evaluation under distribution shift.
method: Roll out the target policy inside a simulator across counterfactual scenarios to generate synthetic trajectories.
Use those simulated trajectories to learn how the system responds to the new policy’s actions.
Evaluate how well predictions learned from simulation transfer to real-world behavior in a Sim2Real setting.
impact: This helps AI/ML practitioners evaluate and forecast policy outcomes earlier, before sufficient real-world data is available. It is especially useful for decision-making systems where collecting on-policy data is expensive, slow, or risky.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline diagram showing historical data, simulator rollouts, and real-world deployment.
A timeline graphic illustrating the cold-start gap before new policy data becomes available.
A flowchart of the Sim2Real process from policy input to simulated trajectories to forecasting model.
An icon-based comparison of simulation vs. reality performance transfer.
paper_title: Forecasting from Counterfactual Simulator Rollouts: A Sim2Real Evaluation
paper_authors: Angel Wang, Dominique Perrault-Joncas, Alvaro Maggiar, Dean Foster, Carson Eisenach
